title: Flexible Work Options
situation: Your company wants to give employees more flexibility. Management is considering two options and has asked all staff to complete a survey before making a decision.
options: Allow employees to work from home two days every week.
Introduce a four-day work week with longer working days.
samples:
I would choose Option A, working from home two days every week. In my opinion, this option would help both the employees and the company more than a four-day week.

First of all, working from home saves a great deal of time. Many of us spend more than an hour travelling to the office and back every day. Without this commute, employees could start work feeling rested, and they would have more time for their families in the evening. They would also save money on gas, parking and lunches.

Secondly, many tasks are easier to do at home. Our office is open and often noisy, so it is hard to concentrate on reports or planning. At home, people can focus on this kind of work without interruptions and then use the office days for meetings and teamwork.

Finally, a four-day week means ten-hour days. I think most people would be too tired to work well by the late afternoon, and parents would have trouble picking up their children on time. For these reasons, I strongly prefer Option A.

I would prefer Option B, a four-day work week with longer days. I believe it would give employees a real break and keep our teams working well together.

The main reason is that a third day off every week would make a big difference to people's lives. Employees could use it for appointments, errands and time with family, so they would not need to leave work early on other days. After a longer weekend, people come back with more energy and a better attitude, which is good for the company too.

Another reason is that everyone would still be in the office at the same time. When people work from home, communication becomes slower, and new employees do not learn as quickly because they cannot simply ask a colleague for help. With a four-day week, we would keep the benefits of working face to face.

Lastly, not everyone has a quiet place to work at home. Some employees live in small apartments or have young children, so working from home would be stressful for them. Therefore, I believe Option B is the fairest choice for all staff.
